section_summary: This section covers Japan’s postwar economic stabilization, including export promotion, fiscal austerity, deconcentration and antitrust policy, and the political effects of the 1949 budget. It also contains correspondence on Far Eastern Commission business, Japanese population and employment, and a despatch assessing an Economic Stabilization Board report. The section ends within that report’s opening discussion.

subfiles.title: Export promotion and economic rehabilitation speech, concluding clipping
subfiles.about: A Japanese government speech urges export priority, restrained consumption, streamlined controls and self-supporting recovery.
subfiles.summary: Concluding page of a speech on export-led recovery and austerity.

subfiles.title: Interpretation of NSC 13/2: Japanese Zaibatsu Policy
subfiles.about: The memorandum seeks decisions on SCAP intervention in reforms and proposed weakening of Japan’s antitrust law.
subfiles.summary: Thorp presents competing readings of NSC 13/2 and opposing views on proposed antitrust amendments. He recommends, if Webb agrees, reaffirming zaibatsu policy, withdrawing the Deconcentration Review Board and delaying legislative changes.

subfiles.title: Japanese Deconcentration
subfiles.about: Thorp forwards the unresolved E–FE policy disagreement on Japanese deconcentration to the Under Secretary.
subfiles.summary: Thorp forwards the zaibatsu policy dispute for decision.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission steering committee meeting of March 29, 1949
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The telegram reports committee discussion of Japanese agrarian reform and several other Far Eastern Commission agenda items.
subfiles.summary: Reports a defeated Soviet request for land-reform information, proposed wording changes to an agrarian reform paper, and deferred discussion of fisheries, assets and other items.

subfiles.title: Political Adviser’s periodic airgram on deconcentration and other matters
subfiles.about: The airgram reports the Review Board’s disavowal of Hutchinson’s Far Eastern Commission statements and mentions Korean trade arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The Board rejects responsibility for Hutchinson’s testimony, while SCAP’s Antitrust and Cartels Division disputes his characterization of enforcement. Later text discusses Korean trade and financial arrangements; pages 116–117 are severely degraded.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning Hutchinson’s deconcentration testimony, draft
subfiles.about: A heavily degraded draft asks about the Board’s refusal to accept responsibility for Hutchinson’s statements.
subfiles.summary: Draft inquiry on the status of Hutchinson’s testimony.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning Hutchinson’s deconcentration testimony
subfiles.about: The Department asks which parts of Hutchinson’s Far Eastern Commission testimony the Review Board disavowed.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests corrected information and clarification of the Board’s position so it can respond to further Far Eastern Commission questions.

subfiles.title: Prime Minister’s Policy Speech of April 4, 1949
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch analyzes Yoshida’s policy speech and the political strain caused by the austerity budget.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida urges economic patriotism and acceptance of the Nine-Point Program. The despatch describes how budget measures contradict Democratic Liberal campaign pledges, expose Finance Minister Ikeda to criticism and complicate Yoshida’s position despite his continued authority.

subfiles.title: Prime Minister Yoshida’s policy speech, Mainichi enclosure
subfiles.about: A newspaper prints Yoshida’s April 4 speech calling for austerity, self-reliance and economic reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida defends the stabilization budget and single exchange rate, urges hard work, and discusses repatriation and Japan’s return to international society.

subfiles.title: Midzuno employment application, record-copy telegram
subfiles.about: SCAP finds that Midzuno’s proposed employment offers no special benefit to Japan or India.
subfiles.summary: SCAP treats Midzuno’s application as a test case for about 200 similar cases.

subfiles.title: Replacement record-copy notice for Tokyo telegram 117
subfiles.about: The form designates a replacement record copy because the original action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: Midzuno employment application, information copy
subfiles.about: A second copy repeats SCAP’s decision on Midzuno’s proposed employment.
subfiles.summary: Information copy of telegram 117 concerning Midzuno.

subfiles.title: Tokyo’s Despatch 215 of April 12, 1949
subfiles.about: Green summarizes the despatch’s account of Yoshida’s budget predicament.
subfiles.summary: Reviews austerity measures and their effect on Yoshida and Ikeda.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Population Problem, transmittal
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser transmits copies of a Japanese Foreign Office population pamphlet.
subfiles.summary: Transmits five copies of Japan’s Population Problem.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Population Problem
subfiles.about: The pamphlet examines population growth, repatriation, employment and possible responses to overpopulation.
subfiles.summary: Using demographic, migration and employment tables, the pamphlet argues that repatriation and postwar births intensified pressure on Japan’s limited resources and depressed living standards. It reviews industrialization, birth control and emigration as possible responses, while warning that projected economic recovery would still leave substantial unemployment. The supplied pages include duplicate table pages and blank pages.

subfiles.title: Political Adviser’s periodic airgram on the Nine-Point Program
subfiles.about: The airgram discusses an Economic and Scientific Section progress report and a proposed Japanese government personnel cut.
subfiles.summary: It reports the Dodge mission’s request for a progress account of Nine-Point Program implementation and SCAP concern about a uniform 30 percent personnel reduction. Pages 173–174 are badly degraded.

subfiles.title: Analysis of Current Economic Situation of Japan, covering despatch
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch summarizes and critiques Economic Stabilization Board reports on Japan’s economy.
subfiles.summary: The despatch notes higher production, slower inflation and rising real wages, but emphasizes import surpluses, weak enterprise finances, deteriorating assets and low living standards. It reviews the Board’s concerns about exchange-rate disparities, falling purchasing power, small firms, controls, wages and fiscal pressure.

subfiles.title: Analysis of Current Economic Situation of Japan
subfiles.about: The report’s opening pages outline signs of stabilization and underlying weaknesses in Japan’s economy.
subfiles.summary: The title, contents and foreword introduce a study of production, inflation, wages, trade deficits, enterprise management, resource depletion and living standards. The opening text argues that apparent stabilization depends heavily on foreign assistance and calls for higher production and exports. The report continues beyond page 185.
